intro: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a federal presidential republic of 31 states and Mexico City. Its presidents serve a single six-year term and can never be re-elected.

chapters.title: One term only
text: The president is elected for one six-year term, called a sexenio, and can never run again. The rule was a reaction to the long dictatorship of Porfirio Díaz, whose re-elections helped spark the revolution. Claudia Sheinbaum of the Morena party took office in 2024.
Congress has a Chamber of Deputies with 500 members and a Senate with 128. In 2025 Mexico became one of the few countries to elect its judges, including Supreme Court justices, by popular vote.

chapters.title: Security
text: Powerful drug cartels control parts of the country, and violence, kidnappings and disappearances are serious problems. The army has taken on a large role in policing, which is controversial.

chapters.title: Flag and symbols
text: The flag is green, white and red with an eagle perched on a cactus, eating a snake. It comes from the Aztec legend that their god told them to build their city where they saw this sign, which they found on an island in Lake Texcoco.
On the night of 15 September, the president rings a bell and repeats Hidalgo's 'cry' of independence from the National Palace, and crowds celebrate across the country.

chapters.title: Mexico in the world
text: Mexico's relationship with the United States, its neighbour and biggest trading partner, dominates its foreign policy, from trade and migration to security. It is a member of the G20 and has strong ties across Latin America.

keyTerms.meaning: A powerful criminal organisation, especially one that smuggles drugs.

cardGroups.title: How power works

items.title: Chamber of Deputies
items.subtitle: 500 deputies
items.text: Makes laws and approves the budget.

items.title: States
items.subtitle: 31 states and Mexico City
items.text: Each with an elected governor and congress.

cardGroups.intro: Who chooses whom, and what each part of the system does.

steps.title: How a law is made
steps.intro: Most new laws follow these steps.

items.title: A bill is proposed
items.text: By the President, members of Congress, state legislatures or citizens.

items.title: First chamber
items.text: Committees review it and the chamber votes.

items.title: Second chamber
items.text: The other chamber reviews and votes.

items.title: The President
items.text: Publishes the law or sends it back with objections.

items.title: Override
items.text: Congress can override with a two-thirds vote.
